packageRules.description: The Go toolchain is declared once, as the `toolchain` directive in go.mod, and the built-in gomod manager proposes bumps for it without configuration. There is deliberately no customManager for a Go version: the one that used to live here could only reach .golangci.yml (its second file pattern, go/.golangci.yml, never existed), so a golang bump moved that file alone while fifteen other declarations stayed behind. The `go` directive is a published compatibility floor for two separately released import paths and moves on a human decision, not a bot's.

A database server image is not an ordinary dependency. Its tag names a release LINE this repository declares in internal/capabilityprobe/cells.go, carrying a capability preset, a support level and -- for a certified line -- a compatibility commitment, so replacing a tag can retire coverage rather than update a dependency. Classify the release before merging. A new LTS or stable line is a candidate for an additional cell, not a replacement for an existing one. A new innovation or current line is an early-signal target. A patch inside a line the matrix already declares is an ordinary update. A line reaching upstream end-of-life is a support-level decision -- legacy-tested if it is worth keeping as a regression sentinel, retired if it is not -- and never an automatic removal, because upstream end-of-life is not Ptah incompatibility. Never auto-merge one of these, and never let a newer image displace a declared line without deciding what happens to that line's cell. TestRenovate_ClassifiesEveryDatabaseServerImage keeps this package list and the declared cells in step.

The clickhouse-legacy integration service is pinned below 24.11 deliberately: CHECK GRANT catalog visibility arrived in 24.11, and TestWriterDropDatabaseRealm_RejectsLegacyServerLive proves the realm-drop guard fails closed without it. Matching on the current value freezes only that pin and leaves the current clickhouse service free to update.
